definitions.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)) and their induced operators on V, indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, X(r)=X_r=x^r/r! in the complex universal enveloping algebra U(sl₂(ℂ)); the same notation denotes its action on V. Powers are compositions on V, with zeroth power the identity.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)) and their induced operators on V, indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, Y(r)=Y_r=y^r/r! in U(sl₂(ℂ)); the same notation denotes its action on V, with zeroth power the identity.
U_Z is the unital ℤ-subalgebra of U(sl₂(ℂ)) generated by X(r) and Y(r) for all integers r≥0, acting on V by its given sl₂(ℂ)-representation.

definitions.type: p-local subring of ℚ, with its usual inclusion in ℂ
definitions.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:a,b∈ℤ, b≠0, p∤b}, with the operations inherited from ℚ and its usual embedding in ℂ.
M_R=R⊗_ℤ M. Its elementary tensors are written r⊗m with r∈R and m∈M.
ι_M(r⊗m)=r m, extending by addition from pure tensors, where R⊂ℂ and M⊂V. When its injectivity has been proved we identify M_R with its image under ι_M.
For i,j∈I, E_ij=E(i,j) is the unique complex-linear operator sending e_j to e_i and e_k to zero for each k∈I with k≠j.
Π=Y(λ)X(λ), with rightmost factor applied first.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K, with K acting on the second tensor factor.

inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, has complex dimension λ+1, and its Chevalley generators x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, both in sl₂(ℂ) and in their actions on V.

M⊂V is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. The lattice is arbitrary; it is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

n=λ+1>0 and |I|=n. The vectors (e_i)_(i∈I) form a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and for t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v. Moreover y^(λ+1)v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. Their action matrices are x e_0=0, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, y e_λ=0; h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i for i∈I. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X(r)e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y(r)e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. Each displayed nonzero coefficient is an integer. Here binom(a,r)=a!/(r!(a−r)!) for integers 0≤r≤a; these are the usual integer binomial coefficients.

For every commutative semiring R₀, additive commutative monoid A with an R₀-module structure, index type Γ, semiring S₀ with an R₀-algebra structure, R₀-basis B:Γ→A, and i∈Γ, the canonical S₀-basis B.baseChange(S₀) of S₀⊗_(R₀)A has ith vector 1⊗B_i. The canonical basis is obtained by tensoring the singleton S₀-basis of S₀ with B and reindexing Γ.

inputs.statement: For every pair of natural numbers u and ℓ, if ℓ is prime, then ℓ divides u! if and only if ℓ≤u.
Every nontrivial commutative ring R₀ satisfies the strong rank condition: for all natural numbers u,w, every injective R₀-linear map R₀^u→R₀^w forces u≤w.

output.statement: R is the subring ℤ_(p) of ℚ⊂ℂ. The map ι_M:R⊗_ℤ M→V is injective. With M_R identified with its image it is a free R-module with an R-basis of n elements and its complex span is V. Each X(r),Y(r), r≥0, preserves M and M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M; ℤx+ℤy+ℤh is closed under the Lie bracket. For every integer 0≤r≤λ, p∤r!, so r! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R and Π=E_λλ, X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ, ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Consequently all E_ij preserve M_R.

locals.type: integer basis of M, also complex basis of V, indexed by a finite set
locals.declaration: Choose an integer basis B of M that is a complex basis of V, as supplied by H004; its index set is finite since V is finite-dimensional by H002.
Choose the simultaneous integer and complex basis m indexed by I provided by F001.
Fix a nonnegative integer r when discussing divided powers, and restrict to r≤λ in S003.

argument.text: Since p is prime by H001, p≥2 and the integers not divisible by p are multiplicatively closed. Fraction addition and multiplication therefore make R a subring of ℚ⊂ℂ; in particular every integer b with p∤b is a unit, with inverse 1/b∈R. By H004 choose a simultaneous integer basis B of M and complex basis B of V. It has finitely many vectors since V has finite dimension n by H002. M010 applied to the nontrivial commutative ring ℂ supplies its strong rank condition. M003 applied to its complex basis gives that its number of vectors is dim_ℂ V=n. By N001, |I|=n; reindexing the basis by I yields the existence stated in F001.

produces.statement: There exists a family m′:I→M which is a ℤ-basis of M and a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Choose m as in F001. Apply M002 with R₀=ℤ, A=M, S₀=R and the integer basis m. It gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_(i∈I) of M_R. The map ι_M sends these basis vectors to m_i; a finite R-linear relation among their images is also a complex-linear relation, so all coefficients are zero. Thus ι_M is injective, identifies M_R with the R-span of the m_i inside V, and its complex span is V. For any r≥0, admissibility H004 and D005 imply X(r)M⊂M and Y(r)M⊂M; R-linearity gives preservation of M_R. In particular X(1)=x and Y(1)=y preserve M; H002 gives h=xy−yx on V, so h preserves M as well. The commutators in H002 show directly that the integer span of x,y,h is bracket-closed, since all three structure constants are integers.

produces.statement: ι_M is injective; the vectors 1⊗m_i form an R-basis of M_R of cardinality n and their images span V over ℂ. For every integer r′≥0, X(r′),Y(r′) preserve M and M_R. Also x,y,h preserve M, and ℤx+ℤy+ℤh is closed under brackets.

argument.text: For every integer 0≤r≤λ, apply M006 with ℓ=p and u=r. H001 supplies primality and r≤λ<p, so p∤r!. Thus r! is a unit of R. In particular λ!, j!, (λ−j)! are all units, for j∈I. Their ratio binom(λ,j)=λ!/[j!(λ−j)!] is a unit of R, with inverse j!(λ−j)!/λ!. The factorials are positive and therefore nonzero as rational numbers. These statements also cover r=0.

produces.statement: For all integers 0≤r′≤λ, p∤r′! and r′! is a unit in R. For every j′∈I, binom(λ,j′) is a unit of R, with inverse j′!(λ−j′)!/λ!.

argument.text: We now identify operators by their actions on the complex basis e from N001. In Y(λ)X(λ), every basis vector below e_λ is killed by X(λ); on e_λ, X(λ)e_λ=e_0 and Y(λ)e_0=e_λ. Hence Π=E_λλ. Next X(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, with coefficient binom(λ−λ+λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ. For ΠY(λ−j), an input e_k with k<j is carried below e_λ and killed by Π; if k>j the lowering string terminates and gives zero; on e_j its coefficient is binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j) and its image is e_λ. Therefore ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. All statements include λ=0, when every factor is the identity on the one-dimensional space.

produces.statement: For all i′,j′∈I, Π=E_λλ, X(λ−i′)Π=E_iλ and ΠY(λ−j′)=binom(λ,j′)E_λj.

argument.text: Combining F004, or applying it to each e_k, gives X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_ij. Invert the coefficient using F003 to get E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F002 and R-linearity, hence every E_ij preserves M_R. With F002 and F003 this proves the entire statement the exported conclusion.
